record.paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
record.original_question: Build an integral input-to-state stability theory for bilinear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded bilinear operators. The paper identifies this part of the theory as still being in its infancy.

evidence.quote: • Integral ISS theory for bilinear systems with unbounded bilinear operators is in its infancy.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a bilinear control system on a Banach space $X$ of the form
$$\dot x(t) = A x(t) + B(u(t), x(t)), \qquad x(0) = x_0 \in X,$$
where $A : D(A) \subset X \to X$ is the generator of a strongly continuous semigroup $(T(t))_{t\ge 0}$ on $X$, $u \in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}([0,\infty); U)$ is an input from a Banach space $U$, and $B : U \times X \to X_{-1}$ is a continuous bilinear map taking values in the extrapolation space $X_{-1}$ associated with $A$ (so that $B$ is, in general, an unbounded bilinear operator with respect to the state space $X$). Mild solutions are defined in $X_{-1}$ and assumed to belong to $X$ for all $t\ge 0$.

The system is called integral input-to-state stable (iISS) if there exist $\beta \in \mathcal{KL}$ and $\theta, \mu \in \mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that for every $x_0 \in X$ and every admissible input $u$,
$$\|x(t)\|_X \le \beta(\|x_0\|_X, t) + \theta\!\left(\int_0^t \mu(\|u(s)\|_U)\, ds\right), \qquad t \ge 0.$$

Develop a systematic integral input-to-state stability theory for such bilinear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded bilinear operators $B$. In particular:

(a) Provide verifiable sufficient conditions on $A$, $B$, $X$, and $U$ ensuring that the system is iISS.
(b) Characterize iISS in terms of qualitative properties such as 0-uniform global asymptotic stability and suitable Lyapunov-type functions adapted to the unbounded setting.
(c) Identify a class of admissible inputs (e.g., subspaces of $L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}$ guaranteeing well-posedness) for which the theory is consistent, and apply the resulting criteria to representative PDE examples with boundary or otherwise unbounded bilinear control.
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress has been made: Hosfeld, Jacob, and Schwenninger (Math. Control Signals Systems, 2022; arXiv:1811.08470) established iISS results for unbounded bilinear control systems on Hilbert spaces, including sufficient conditions and applications such as a bilinearly controlled Fokker–Planck equation. Subsequent work has extended ISS/iISS estimates to bilinear feedback systems with applications to viscous Burgers, Schrödinger, Navier–Stokes, and semilinear wave equations. However, a fully general theory covering arbitrary unbounded bilinear operators on Banach spaces is not yet complete, so the program is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Integral input-to-state stability of unbounded bilinear control systems
status_evidence.snippet: Studies integral input-to-state stability of bilinear systems with unbounded control operators and provides natural sufficient conditions; applies to bilinearly controlled Fokker–Planck equation.
status_evidence.claim: Substantial progress on iISS for bilinear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded operators.

status_evidence.title: [1811.08470] Integral input-to-state stability of unbounded bilinear control systems
status_evidence.snippet: Hosfeld, Jacob, Schwenninger develop iISS criteria for unbounded bilinear control systems.
status_evidence.claim: Direct partial resolution of the open problem.

status_evidence.title: Input-to-state stability for bilinear feedback systems
status_evidence.snippet: ISS estimates for infinite-dimensional bilinear feedback systems with applications to Burgers, Schrödinger, Navier-Stokes, semilinear wave equations.
status_evidence.claim: Further progress in the bilinear ISS/iISS theory.
